key_insight: LandscapeSHAP gives Shapley-value credit to individual persistence diagram points behind persistence landscape features, and for linear models this credit has a closed form.
engineering_relevance: This makes topological data analysis models more interpretable by tracing a prediction back to specific homology classes, with scalable approximation for larger diagrams.
method: Derive an exact closed-form Shapley value for linear models on persistence landscapes.
Use the Shapley axioms to uniquely define credit allocation for any model type.
Approximate the intractable 2^N coalition average with Monte Carlo sampling and convergence rates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports exact theory for linear models plus sampling-based approximation and convergence guarantees, but no empirical dataset benchmark is described.
watch_item: Exact computation for nonlinear models remains exponential in the number of persistence diagram points, so Monte Carlo approximation may still be costly for large diagrams.
paper_title: LandscapeSHAP: Which Persistent Homology Class Gets the Credit?
